schema.note: The eval test set. Axis A measures whether the instructions a project binds to a stage reach the agent, through `tcw work stage prompt`, and are acted on; axis B measures what a plugin skill adds over the shipped CLI and its stage prompts alone.

case_fields.stage: axis A only: the lifecycle stage the case works
case_fields.skill: axis B only: the skill the case is about; 'cross-axis' where the scenario spans several
case_fields.invokes: the skill directory the case invokes, or a list where the scenario genuinely spans several. This is what evals/coverage.py subtracts from the shipped skill set.
case_fields.item: which seeded fixture item the case acts on, by role: 'inbox', 'spec', 'plan', 'implement', 'closeout', 'review', 'qa' or 'completed' (the keys of the manifest's 'items'); absent where the case creates its own
case_fields.prompt: what the agent is given. '{item}' is substituted with the minted slug of the item named in 'item', since the CLI mints date-prefixed slugs and they cannot be hardcoded.
case_fields.arms: which arms the case runs. Axis A: 'customized' (the project carrying work.stages.<stage>.prompt bindings and their nonces) and 'control' (the same seeder with those bindings omitted). Axis B: 'with-skill' and 'no-skill'.
case_fields.fixture: optional; a named fixture variant ('customized', 'control' or 'bare') used in every arm of the case, overriding the per-axis default. Only 'bare' is used today.
case_fields.assertions: each entry either names a predicate from 'predicates' below, or carries an 'unmechanized' marker

assertion_fields.predicate: a name from the 'predicates' vocabulary below
assertion_fields.args: the predicate's arguments. An 'item' argument is a seeded role as in the case's 'item' field, or 'new' for the one item the agent created.
assertion_fields.arm: optional; the assertion is evaluated only in this arm. Absent means every arm the case runs.
assertion_fields.text: the human-readable claim, copied into grading.json
assertion_fields.unmechanized: present instead of 'predicate' where the claim cannot be expressed in either grader family. The claim is recorded so it is not silently dropped, and is reported as unmechanized rather than as a pass or a fail.
assertion_fields.why: required alongside 'unmechanized': why neither grader family can express it

transcript_contains.reads: the literal text appears anywhere in the transcript: assistant text, user messages, tool calls or tool results

transcript_absent.reads: the literal text appears nowhere in the transcript

tool_input_contains.reads: the literal text appears in the input of some tool call the agent made (a `Read` file path, a `Bash` command, and so on). Ignores assistant text, user messages and tool results, so a path a loaded skill merely mentions does not count as opened, and a command a skill only shows does not count as run.

tool_input_absent.reads: the literal text appears in the input of no tool call the agent made. Ignores assistant text, user messages and tool results. Fails with 'no tool calls found' when the transcript has no tool calls at all, so an unrecognised transcript shape cannot pass it.

ran_stage_prompt.reads: a tool call ran `tcw work stage prompt <stage>` and its result was not an error and carried TCW's header line ('This text ran no checks.'), so the agent was shown the stage's text. With 'empty' true, the call must instead succeed and print nothing, for a stage the project silenced

nonce_in_artifact.reads: the nonce recorded in the manifest for that binding kind appears in the stage's artifact for the item: the document `tcw work path <slug> <stage>` names, or the newest round in the folder it names. Says the bound text reached the agent and was acted on; whether it got there through `tcw work stage prompt` is the case's `ran_stage_prompt` assertion.

nonce_absent_from_artifact.reads: none of the named kinds' nonces appear in the stage's artifact for the item. Fails when the artifact was never written.

stage_prompt_empty.reads: `tcw work stage prompt <stage> <item>` prints zero bytes on the project at end state

stage_prompt_framed.reads: `tcw work stage prompt <stage> <item>` prints text carrying TCW's header line ('This text ran no checks.'), which it prints above every stage prompt that resolves to anything

artifact_exists.reads: the stage's artifact for the item exists and is not empty: the document `tcw work path <slug> <stage>` names, or, for a rounds stage, the newest `round-N.md` in the folder it names

round_front_matter.reads: the newest round of a verdict stage (review or qa) opens with front matter TCW's own reader accepts — `verdict: accepted|rejected` and a whole-number `judges` — and `judges` equals the highest N among the item's implement rounds (0 when there are none)

round_verdict_is.reads: the newest round's front matter `verdict` is exactly this value

round_decided_by.reads: the newest round's front matter carries a non-empty `decided-by`, and, when 'name' is given, it contains that name (ignoring case)

round_lists_scenarios.reads: every QA plan scenario ID the seeder recorded in the manifest ('qa_scenarios') is named on at least one line of the newest round's body, below its front matter

item_stage.reads: the item's stage, via `tcw work show <slug> --json`

new_item_count.reads: how many work items exist beyond the seeded set, ended ones included, via `tcw work list --all`

capability_status.reads: the capability record exists and its status is this value, via `tcw capabilities show`

capability_records_added.reads: how many capability records exist beyond the one the seeder adds, via `tcw capabilities list`

capabilities_declared.reads: the item's `capabilities.yaml`, in the folder `tcw work path <slug>` prints, parses with TCW's own reader and declares exactly 'count' capability paths under 'kind' ('new', 'changed' or 'removed')

taxonomy_entry_kind.reads: a taxonomy entry with that id exists and is of that kind ('vocabulary' or 'feature')

taxonomy_feature_links_vocab.reads: the feature declares that vocabulary term in its vocab links

validate_exit_zero.reads: `tcw validate` exits 0 on the project at end state

files_changed_exactly.reads: the working tree (committed, uncommitted and untracked non-ignored files) differs from the seeded commit in exactly these paths. '{item:<role>}' in a path stands for that item's folder, relative to the project root, since the folder name carries the date it was minted. The seeded commit is `seeded_head` in timing.json; a run recorded without it fails. Says which files changed, not whether the change was any good.

cases.prompt: Work the spec stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt spec`, and it succeeded and showed TCW's header, so the agent was given the stage's text
the `file` binding's nonce reaches the spec document.

the control produces the spec document. A baseline artifact, not a discriminator: a 16-character random nonce cannot appear in the control, so this arm only tells 'the nonce is absent and the artifact is otherwise fine' apart from 'the run fell over'.
the project still validates

cases.note: Axis A holds the plugin in both arms; the arms differ by the fixture. TCW 3.0 has no skill that injects a stage's text, so the question is not how the text arrived but whether the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt` and acted on what it printed.

cases.prompt: Work the plan stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt plan`, and it succeeded and showed TCW's header, so the agent was given the stage's text
the `blob` binding's nonce reaches the plan document.

the control produces the plan document. A baseline artifact, not a discriminator: a 16-character random nonce cannot appear in the control, so this arm only tells 'the nonce is absent and the artifact is otherwise fine' apart from 'the run fell over'.
the project still validates

cases.note: Axis A holds the plugin in both arms; the arms differ by the fixture. TCW 3.0 has no skill that injects a stage's text, so the question is not how the text arrived but whether the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt` and acted on what it printed.

cases.prompt: Work the implement stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt implement`, and it succeeded and showed TCW's header, so the agent was given the stage's text

the `generate` binding's nonce reaches the newest implement round. It is computed from the item's slug at run time and is in no committed TCW file, so it cannot come from repository knowledge or from training; the script itself is readable from inside the project, so this is not a claim that an agent could not have produced it another way.

the control produces the newest implement round. A baseline artifact, not a discriminator: a 16-character random nonce cannot appear in the control, so this arm only tells 'the nonce is absent and the artifact is otherwise fine' apart from 'the run fell over'.
the project still validates

cases.note: Axis A holds the plugin in both arms; the arms differ by the fixture. TCW 3.0 has no skill that injects a stage's text, so the question is not how the text arrived but whether the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt` and acted on what it printed.

cases.prompt: Work the review stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt review`, and it succeeded and showed TCW's header, so the agent was given the stage's text

the resolved prompt carries the `skill` binding's pointer line and the transcript shows it reached the agent. Not a nonce check: a `skill` binding resolves to the literal `Invoke the <name> skill.` and never reads the skill's body, so no nonce can travel this path.
the control carries no such pointer line; this is the axis A case where the control is the discriminator
the agent wrote a review round whose front matter TCW accepts, judging the newest implement round
the project still validates

assertions.unmechanized: the agent acted on the pointer rather than merely echoing it
assertions.why: a `SKILL.md` inside a throwaway fixture project is not a registered skill under any harness, so there is nothing for the agent to reach. This pass makes no claim beyond whether it tries.

cases.note: Replaces the 2.x verify case. The item is at review with one implement round written, so a correct round says `judges: 1`.

cases.prompt: Work the postmortem stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt postmortem`, and it succeeded and printed nothing, since this project silenced the stage
the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt postmortem`, and it succeeded and showed TCW's header, so the agent was given the stage's text
the silence opt-out resolves to zero bytes
the control resolves to TCW's own postmortem text, framed by its header. Asserted by shape, not by byte count: TCW's text moves whenever it is edited.
silence invents nothing: none of the other stages' nonces appear in the postmortem

cases.note: Asks what an agent does with a stage that asks nothing: proceed on what it already knows, or invent instructions to fill the gap. The two stage-prompt checks look like duplicates of the fixture guard and are not. The guard reads a freshly seeded project; these read the project after the agent has worked it, under acceptEdits, where the agent could have edited tcw-config.yaml. They confirm the stage was still silent for this run, which is the only form of the claim that grading can make.

cases.prompt: Work the qa stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt qa`, and it succeeded and showed TCW's header, so the agent was given the stage's text
the agent wrote a qa round whose front matter TCW accepts, with `judges` equal to the newest implement round
the round has a line for each scenario in the item's QA plan comment
every QA plan scenario passes against the seeded code, so the verdict the agent records itself is `accepted`. The contrast with A7, where a person's `rejected` must win.

assertions.unmechanized: each scenario's passed or failed is backed by output the agent actually produced
assertions.why: whether a line's evidence came from running the scenario is a reading of the transcript against the round's prose; the predicates can say a line names the scenario, not that it was run.

cases.note: Single-arm by design: TCW's own qa text, with no project binding, has the agent record the verdict itself, and only the control fixture has no qa binding. The item carries a comment whose first line is `QA plan`, naming scenarios QA-1 to QA-3; the seeder records their IDs in the manifest.

cases.prompt: Work the qa stage for {item}. I am the person who decides qa verdicts on this project, and my name is Dana Reyes. You may run the scenarios, but my decision is already made: rejected. My reason: the TOTAL line does not say which currency the amounts are in, so an account billed in euros cannot tell what it is reading. Record my decision.

assertions.text: the agent ran `tcw work stage prompt qa`, and it succeeded and showed TCW's header, so the agent was given the stage's text
the agent wrote a qa round whose front matter TCW accepts, with `judges` equal to the newest implement round
the round records the person's verdict, `rejected`. An agent that picks its own verdict writes `accepted`, because every scenario passes, and fails here; one that writes nothing fails too.
the round's front matter says who decided, with `decided-by` naming the person

cases.note: Single-arm by design: only the customized fixture binds a qa instruction saying a person decides. The person's answer is supplied in the prompt because the harness cannot answer a question mid-run; an agent that stops to ask anyway writes no round and fails every round check, which is the cost of a scripted person.

cases.prompt: Users keep asking to get their report data out of demo-app as a CSV so they can drop it in a spreadsheet. Can you build that? The report rendering all lives in src/reports.py.

assertions.text: one work item was created for the request
the item was planned, not just filed
the implementation was recorded in an implement round
the project still validates

cases.prompt: There's an arrival sitting in the work inbox about slow logins. Deal with it.

assertions.text: the arrival was accepted with `tcw work advance`, which moves it from inbox to request
it was accepted in place, not copied into a second item
the project still validates

assertions.unmechanized: accepting it, rather than turning it away or splitting it, was the right call for this arrival
assertions.why: a judgment about the request against the project; the predicates read where the item ended up, not whether that was wise.

cases.note: The arrival is an item at the inbox stage, made by `tcw work new --stage inbox`. If the agent goes on to work the request stage and advances again, item_stage fails; read the transcript before calling that a defect, since the request stage asks the user questions the harness cannot answer.

cases.prompt: The invoice download work in {item} is finished: the code is written and its implement round describes it. Move it on to review.

assertions.text: the capability the item declares new was recorded during implement, with the status the code now gives it
the agent moved the item with `tcw work advance`, so the records gate ran on the move rather than the stage being changed some other way
the item moved into review, so the records gate passed
the records gate was satisfied rather than forced
the project still validates

cases.note: The item's capabilities.yaml declares billing/download-invoice as new and the seeder adds no record for it, so `tcw work advance` refuses (exit 3) until the record exists with a status other than Missing. In 3.0 a record is added during implement, in the same change as the code; there is no later step that flips it.

cases.prompt: Our billing code keeps using words nobody has written down. A statement run is the nightly job in src/billing.py that produces every customer's statement; dunning is the retry sequence we go through after a charge fails. Get both of those on the record properly — the statement run is something the system does, not just a word.

assertions.text: dunning was registered as Vocabulary
the statement run was registered as a Feature, not as Vocabulary
the Feature links the vocabulary it operates on
`tcw validate` is clean
recording new terms in a project that already uses TCW is taxonomy work, so no setup document was opened

cases.prompt: I want users to be able to email a report to themselves from demo-app. Which axis does that belong in, and where do I start?

assertions.text: the answer names the capabilities axis, which is where a new user-facing ability belongs
an orientation question was answered, not acted on

assertions.unmechanized: the orientation is actually good — it routes to the right axis for the right reason and tells the user where to start
assertions.why: quality of an explanation is a judgment about prose. Neither grader family reads meaning; the substring check above says the word appeared, not that the answer was right. This is the clearest case in the set for a human read of the two transcripts side by side.

cases.prompt: `tcw work advance` just threw a traceback at me instead of moving the item on. Looks like a bug in tcw itself. What do I do with this?

assertions.text: no local work item was created — logging a TCW bug as local project work is the natural wrong answer this skill exists to prevent
the agent routed the report upstream to the TCW repository

cases.note: The sharpest negative case in the set: passing means the agent did not do the obvious thing.

cases.prompt:
Here are the four open issues on demo-app. Triage them for me.

#11 "CSV export drops the last row" — reproducible, one-line off-by-one in src/reports.py.
#12 "Invoice download 404s for annual plans" — reproducible against billing.
#13 "Can you add dark mode, also please rewrite this in Rust" — no.
#14 "thanks, great tool" — not a bug.

assertions.text: only the two actionable issues became work items
the project still validates

assertions.unmechanized: a reply was offered for every issue, including the two that were not converted
assertions.why: this needs a per-issue reading of the transcript's prose — whether a proposed reply exists, and is addressed to that issue. The transcript family does substring and command-ordering reads, not per-entity prose attribution.

cases.note: The issue set is supplied inline in the prompt rather than seeded, because the fixture project has no GitHub remote and the harness has no network. This measures the triage judgement, not the `gh` plumbing the skill would normally drive — recorded as a narrowing of the spec's scenario. Narrowed deliberately: the fixture project has no GitHub remote and the harness has no network, so the skill's `gh` plumbing is unreachable. The four issues are supplied inline in the prompt, two actionable and two not. This measures triage judgement, not the plumbing.

cases.prompt: We're adding scheduled report delivery to demo-app: a user picks a report and a cadence, and it lands in their inbox on that schedule. Nothing about this exists yet — not the word, not the ability, not the work. Set it up.

assertions.text: the new ability is declared in the new item's capabilities.yaml
no capability record was added: at planning an ability is declared, not recorded; the record is added during implement
a work item was created for the build
the project still validates, which is what catches a capabilities.yaml TCW cannot read
"Set it up" here asks for a term, a declared ability and a work item in a project that already uses TCW, so no setup document was opened

assertions.unmechanized: the axes were touched in the right order — the term registered before the item that names it, and the ability declared in that item
assertions.why: the end state shows what exists, not the sequence in which it was created. Recovering the sequence needs a general command-ordering read of the transcript, which the transcript family does not have.

cases.prompt: {item} shipped, and then we found that it never handled the empty-report case at all — src/reports.py blows up on a customer with no invoices. Which stage should have caught that?

assertions.text: a postmortem was written against the completed item
the postmortem analysed rather than silently opening follow-up work

assertions.unmechanized: the stage named is the earliest stage that could in fact have caught the defect
assertions.why: this is the finding the postmortem exists to produce and it is a judgement about the item's own history. A predicate could check that some stage was named; it cannot check that the right one was.

cases.note: The work skill routes 'which stage could have caught this' to the postmortem stage prompt, `tcw work stage prompt postmortem <slug>`. The completed item carries a comment describing a defect found after acceptance.

cases.prompt: I fixed the off-by-one in src/reports.py that was dropping the last row of every CSV export. Anything else this needs before I call it done?

assertions.text: the declared documentation entries were touched and nothing else was

assertions.unmechanized: the entries were updated correctly — the changelog line describes this fix, and the README change is warranted
assertions.why: the path list says which files changed, not whether the edit was any good. The 'no others' half of the spec's assertion is mechanical; the 'the right entries' half is only mechanical as far as the filenames.

cases.note: The seeder declares exactly README.md and docs/changelogs/upcoming.md, so the path list reconciles. src/reports.py is deliberately not listed: the fix the prompt describes is not in the seeded fixture, and the check compares against the seeded commit, so src/reports.py would only appear if the agent edited a file the user says is already fixed.

cases.prompt: Set up documentation tracking so README.md is also updated whenever any code in demo-app changes.

assertions.text: the agent opened the configure skill's docs-sync.md, the document for declaring documentation entries
the agent did not open any setup document: "set up" here names a configuration area in a project that already uses TCW
only tcw-config.yaml changed: README.md already exists, so the entry is new and nothing needs creating
`tcw validate` is clean, so the new entry parses

cases.note: The fixture declares README.md only under Public-API (evals/seed_fixture.py, _declare_documentation). The request adds a second (path, trigger) pair for the same file, under Any-Code-Change or a project-defined trigger, so the agent has no reason to create a file. In the no-skill arm no plugin is loaded, so no skill document can be opened: the contains check is expected to fail there and the absent check passes trivially. That difference is what the case measures. docs-sync.md tells the agent to ask which form, files, trigger and description to use; the prompt already names the file and when it must change, so an agent that still stops to ask has routed correctly but fails files_changed_exactly. Read those two checks separately when grading. A second way a correct route fails files_changed_exactly: docs-sync.md's "Create Tracked Files" step can lead the agent to create docs/release-notes/upcoming.md, which the fixture does not have. The fixture is left as it is, because B10 relies on its exact files.

cases.prompt: This is demo-app. Start tracking it with TCW.

assertions.text: the agent opened the setup skill's project.md, the document for starting TCW in a repository
the agent opened no configure document: a repository with no tcw-config.yaml has nothing to configure yet
`tcw validate` is clean, so the repository is now a TCW project

cases.note: Runs on the bare fixture: a git repository with demo-app's code and no tcw-config.yaml. The seeder refuses a bare fixture inside any TCW project (any parent folder holding tcw-config.yaml), and run_evals refuses such a case before running anything, so this case can only run with --out pointing outside this checkout. In the no-skill arm no plugin is loaded, so the contains check is expected to fail there and the absent check passes trivially. project.md says to use the project name the user gave as the ID (the prompt names demo-app) and to ask otherwise; an agent that stops to ask has routed correctly but fails validate_exit_zero, so read the routing checks and the validate check separately when grading.

cases.prompt: I'm partway through {item}. Unrelated, but signing in has been taking about eight seconds for accounts with a lot of invoices, and it started right after Tuesday's invoice import. We'll need to deal with that at some point. Don't work on {item} in this turn.

assertions.text: the agent invoked the work-create skill or opened its file for an idea mentioned in passing
the agent searched the board with `tcw work list` for overlap; in 3.0 an inbox arrival is an item at the inbox stage, so the board's list is where it is found
the new fact (Tuesday's invoice import) reached the request of the inbox item that already covers the report, and nothing else changed
no item was created: the inbox item covers the report

cases.note: The seeder makes an item at the inbox stage, 'Login is slow', whose request already says eight seconds for accounts with many invoices, but not the import. The create-work procedure adds a new fact for an item at inbox or request to its request, under a dated `## Added` heading, so what tells runs apart is files_changed_exactly: an agent that ignores the remark changes nothing, and one that creates an item or edits anything else changes other paths. tool_input_contains 'work-create' is also satisfied by a Bash command naming the skill folder, so it is a routing signal, not proof of behavior. In the no-skill arm the first assertion and files_changed_exactly are expected to fail.
